root_cause: TWO DEFECTS, BOTH REQUIRED. (1) THE RENEWAL NEVER RAN. stayconnect-hotel-admin-cert-renew.service declares ExecStart=/usr/local/sbin/stayconnect-hotel-admin-cert-manager; nothing ever installed that file. The timer fired daily from 2026-08-22 and every firing failed 203/EXEC. The installer guard written to prevent exactly this - after the backup-cleanup outage - scanned only /opt/stayconnect/bin paths, so a unit naming /usr/local/sbin was invisible to it and it reported OK throughout. (2) THE HEALTH MODEL COULD NOT SEE THE FAILURE. The LEAF never expired: it was minted 2026-08-20 and runs to 2028, and status.json correctly said 'healthy, days_remaining 729' the entire time. What expired on 2026-08-27 was the INTERMEDIATE pinned inside the served fullchain. Caddy's local authority issues SEVEN-DAY intermediates and rotates them in its own storage, but this vhost serves a static fullchain file, so the chain captured at mint time rots weekly however long the leaf lives. `openssl x509 -in <fullchain>` reads only the FIRST certificate, so every question the manager asked - valid? near expiry? days remaining? - was answered by the leaf alone. NOT the cause: the Root CA (healthy, untouched), the leaf's own validity, SAN configuration, or Caddy itself.
root_ca: UNCHANGED, AND DELIBERATELY SO. 'Caddy Local Authority - 2026 ECC Root', serial 990DFBFF2B14A2A84F56D2EB9A655418, valid 2026-08-20 to 2036-06-28, SHA-256 fingerprint 55:70:7E:AE:7C:E6:04:48:CE:D0:BF:C8:B9:C1:97:E1:9F:41:97:90:BA:95:46:A1:67:ED:DF:34:F7:2F:68:75. It was verified healthy BEFORE anything was touched and its fingerprint is identical afterwards. Nothing was regenerated, replaced or rotated at the CA level: an expired leaf - or in this case an expired intermediate - is not a reason to disturb a root that ten years of trust distribution depends on.

Its chain carries Caddy's current intermediate and verifies against the unchanged root.
fixes: The manager is now CHAIN-AWARE: chain_expiring() examines every certificate in the served fullchain and chain_verifies() confirms the file as served still chains to the local root, both in needs_renewal and in the candidate validation, so a chain that cannot be used can no longer be called healthy. A separate CHAIN_RENEW_DAYS window (2 days) tracks the intermediate's own clock rather than the leaf's, because a 45-day window measured against a two-year leaf renews years after the seven-day intermediate has gone. The installer now verifies EVERY absolute Exec path any unit declares, in any directory, and installs helpers whose units name a path outside /opt/stayconnect/bin - deriving the source from the unit's own path so a new location cannot silently produce another 203/EXEC service.
verification: The renewal ran through the managed lifecycle and Caddy now serves serial 35F2CBA4... - confirmed by reading the certificate off the live TLS socket, not from disk. Strict verification passes BOTH ways against the existing root with no bypass: by DNS SAN (--resolve hotel.stayconnect.local) and by IP SAN (https://172.21.60.25), each ssl_verify_result=0, http=200. The renewal UNIT (not the script) then ran and exited 0/SUCCESS as a safe no-op - 'no-op: valid and correct' with the serial unchanged - proving the repair holds when the certificate is outside its renewal window. The timer is active with its next run scheduled. status.json now records last_renewal_result=renewal_succeeded and retry_count=0.
insecure_bypass_removed: HOTEL_ADMIN_PUBLIC_INSECURE is GONE from /etc/stayconnect/hotel-admin-integrity.env. The standing check now uses HOTEL_ADMIN_PUBLIC_CACERT pointing at the existing local root and --resolve so the request carries the real vhost name while reaching the management IP - which makes the DNS SAN part of the proof rather than an assumption. No -k and no verification bypass remains in the healthy configuration.
